devdoc.details: The maximum time to maturity is 100 years.Markets have at most 128 collaterals.Collaterals list must be sorted by collateral address (ascending, no duplicates), and not empty.Within a market, a borrower can use at most MAX_COLLATERALS_PER_BORROWER (16) collaterals simultaneously.The case LLTV = 1 is special, and should be used with care, notably: - It has no overcollateralization, so unhealthy positions will almost always realize bad debt when liquidated. In particular, the RCF (see LIQUIDATIONS section) is "inactive", meaning liquidations can always liquidate everything. - It has no liquidation incentive, so liquidators repay at exactly the oracle price (plus roundings).To check if a market has been touched, check if tickSpacing(marketId) > 0.When some assets become withdrawable before maturity (after a repayment or a liquidation), there is an incentive to take resting sell offers with price < 1 (more precisely price < 1 - settlementFee) and withdraw instantly. Lenders (and the fee claimer) might also race to withdraw first. MULTI-COLLATERAL MARKETSBorrowers can supply/withdraw their collaterals at any time, subject only to a health check on withdrawal. In particular, the borrowers of multi-collateral markets can completely change their collateral composition.Liquidation reverts if any of the activated collaterals' oracle reverts (see LIVENESS).The oracle-quoted liquidator incentive (i.e., maxRepayable * (LIF-1)) might not be constant across activated collaterals. Hence, liquidators may have a preference order over collaterals when liquidating. SETTLEMENT FEESA default settlement fee (per loan token) is set on new markets. Then, the fee setter can override it.The settlement fee is a piecewise linear function on the TTM (time to maturity). It is computed with linear approximation between breakpoints.Settlement fee breakpoint indices: 0=0d, 1=1d, 2=7d, 3=30d, 4=90d, 5=180d, 6=360d.For TTM > 360d, the settlement fee is the fee at the 360d breakpoint.Post-maturity, the settlement fee is the fee at the 0d breakpoint.Settlement fees are stored in cbp (centi-basis-points): settlementFee / CBP.One cbp is 1e-6 WAD, i.e. 0.01 bps. This fits each breakpoint in 16 bits.Max settlement fee is defined per index: 50 bps for ttm=360 days, scaled linearly (except for 0d, 0.14 bps). CONTINUOUS FEESA default continuous fee (per loan token) is set on new markets. Then, the fee setter can override it.The fee is tracked per lender via pendingFee in each position. If the market's continuous fee changes, the pending fee of existing lenders is not updated (=> their fee is fixed). If the market's continuous fee is decreased lenders might self-take to exit and re-enter to reduce their pending fee (at the cost of the settlement fee).In the absence of bad debt realizations, the face value of a lender's position is credit - pendingFee.An offer cannot be taken if its continuousFeeCap value is lower than the current market continuous fee. This ensures maker buyers can protect against future continuous fee increases. LIQUIDATIONSAccounts are liquidatable only if they are either unhealthy or the maturity has passed. The liquidation shouldn't be locked either.Liquidations are locked for the seller during the callbacks of take.Liquidations can revert for other reasons, see LIVENESS.There are two liquidation modes: The "post-maturity mode", available after the market's maturity, and the "normal mode", available if the borrower is unhealthy. After maturity, an unhealthy borrower's liquidator can choose between both modes.In the "normal mode", the liquidation incentive factor (LIF) is the computed maxLif and the liquidation amount is capped by what is needed to put back the position into health ("recovery close factor", or "RCF").The RCF condition is (omitting scaling and roundings):   newDebt >= newMaxDebt <=> debt - repaidUnits >= maxDebt - repaidUnits*LIF*LLTV                         <=> repaidUnits <= (debt-maxDebt) / (1 - LIF*LLTV).maxRepaid is rounded up such that it doesn't prevent to liquidate enough to put back the account into health.When LIF*LLTV = 1, repaying never restores health, so the RCF is inactive and the whole position can be liquidated.The RCF is deactivated for small collateral amount, essentially to mitigate issues with liquidations that are too small compared to the gas cost. More precisely, it is deactivated if the liquidation could leave a collateral with a value that would not be enough to repay rcfThreshold units. Which means (omitting scaling and roundings):   minNewCollateral * liquidatedCollatPrice / LIF < rcfThreshold     <=> (collateral - maxRepaid * LIF / liquidatedCollatPrice) * liquidatedCollatPrice / LIF < rcfThreshold     <=> collateral * liquidatedCollatPrice / LIF - maxRepaid < rcfThresholdNothing prevents borrowers from opening small positions / takers and liquidators from leaving small positions that might not be profitable to liquidate because of gas cost. The RCF deactivation at rcfThreshold just prevents the systemic aspect (liquidations with RCF progressively reducing the position's sizes).In the "post-maturity mode", the LIF (liquidation incentive factor) grows linearly from 1 at maturity to the computed maxLif at maturity + TIME_TO_MAX_LIF, and the RCF is deactivated.In both modes, maxLif is used to determine if the account has some bad debt, to always assume the worst case. SLASHINGWhen a borrower's bad debt is realized, it is socialized among lenders in this market.At each lender's next interaction, their credit is slashed proportionally. GROUPSGroups are useful to have a global offered amount shared across multiple offers ("One cancels the other").To work as expected, all offers in the same group should have the same maker, direction (offer.buy), max values and loan token. OFFER SIZEExactly one of maxAssets or maxUnits must be nonzero per offer (take reverts otherwise).maxAssets caps max buyer assets if offer.buy is true, and caps max seller assets otherwise.If maxAssets > 0, assets are capped to maxAssets, otherwise units are capped to maxUnits.Midnight can call the callback of offers through a take, even if those offers have consumed==max.Fully consumed assets-based offers can still be taken for nonzero units when the asset amount added to consumed is zero.consumed can be increased manually by the maker or authorized accounts.Offers that do not want to set a limit should set their max to type(uint128).max - 1 so that they can be fully canceled by setting consumed to type(uint128).max. TICK SPACINGOffers can only be placed at ticks that are multiples of the market's spacing.Newly created markets start at the global DEFAULT_TICK_SPACING.The tickSpacingSetter can decrease the spacing to a divisor of the current spacing, unlocking new ticks only. AUTHORIZATIONSAll functions that change the position, consumed and authorization are accessible to the user and to any account that has been authorized. Thus, to scope authorizations one should authorize a smart-contract with scoped behavior.When authorizing a smart-contract, one should consider: - The targets/functions that the account can call. At least Midnight's functions should be considered, but other contracts might re-use Midnight's authorization mapping too (e.g ratifiers and authorizers). In particular, authorized accounts can authorize other accounts on behalf of the user. - Under which conditions the account can return CALLBACK_SUCCESS when its isRatified function is called.updatePosition and liquidate (for liquidatable users) also impact the position and are permissionless. ROUNDINGSassets are rounded against the taker and in favor of the maker in take (in particular a take with non-zero units could end up with buyerAssets or sellerAssets equal to zero). Therefore, the settlement fee has no defined rounding direction, which could lead to fees manipulations on chains with very cheap gas.pendingFee updates are rounded in favor of the user. It could lead to fees manipulations too.maxDebt is rounded down in isHealthy and liquidate.lossFactor is rounded up so lenders collectively lose a bit more than badDebt on each bad debt realization.If a market loses almost all of its value to bad debt over its lifetime, then the accounting of the loss may become extremely imprecise (against the user), potentially leading to a total loss. Note that the take function reverts when the loss factor is maxed out.updatePosition rounds credit down, so each lender loses a bit at their next interaction after a bad debt realization.repaidUnits/seizedAssets computations round against the liquidator. GATESGates are optional (address(0) = unrestricted).The entry gate can prevent increasing credit or debt in the market.In particular, it does not prevent the user from exiting the market even when the entry gate is reverting.The liquidator gate can prevent the user from liquidating borrowers in the market (and realizing bad debt). TOKEN SAFETY REQUIREMENTSList of assumptions on tokens that guarantee that Midnight behaves as expected: - It should be ERC-20 compliant, except that it can omit return values on transfer and transferFrom. In particular, it should not revert because a transfer is no-op. - Midnight's balance of the token should only decrease on transfer and transferFrom. - It should not re-enter Midnight on transfer nor transferFrom. - Midnight must send/receive exactly the requested amount on transfers.See LIVENESS for liveness guarantees. LIVENESSIf an activated collateral oracle reverts on price, liquidate reverts.If the supplied collateral oracle reverts on price, the activation of that collateral through supplyCollateral reverts.If an activated collateral oracle reverts on price, isHealthy, withdrawCollateral and take revert when the user (seller for take) has non-zero debt.If the liquidated collateral oracle returns 0 on price, liquidate with repaid input reverts.If an activated collateral oracle returns a price such that the user's collateral quoted in loan token is greater than type(uint128).max, then liquidate, isHealthy, withdrawCollateral when the borrower has debt, and take whenever the seller still has debt could revert.If enterGate.canIncreaseCredit reverts or returns false, take reverts if the buyer's credit increases.If enterGate.canIncreaseDebt reverts or returns false, take reverts if the seller's debt increases.If liquidatorGate.canLiquidate reverts or returns false, liquidate reverts.If a token pulled by Midnight reverts or returns false on transferFrom, take, repay, supplyCollateral, liquidate, and flashLoan repayment revert when they need to pull that token.If a token sent by Midnight reverts or returns false on transfer, withdraw, withdrawCollateral, fee claims, liquidate, and flashLoan revert when they need to send that token.If a callback reverts or returns something other than CALLBACK_SUCCESS, take, repay, liquidate, and flashLoan revert. ROLESThe configurator can set the configurator, fee setter, fee claimer, and tick spacing setter, as well as enable LLTV tiers and liquidation cursors.The fee setter can set the default and per-market settlement fee and continuous fee.The fee claimer can claim the settlement fee and continuous fee.When the claimer is set, the old claimer loses the unclaimed fees.The tick spacing setter can decrease the tick spacing of a market. MISCNo-ops are allowed.Zero checks are not systematically performed.NatSpec comments are included only when they bring clarity.credit, pendingFee, and lastLossFactor are not up to date. Use updatePositionView to get the up-to-date values.The max amount of totalUnits, collateral, credit, continuousFeeCredit and debt is type(uint128).max (~1e38).Markets use their creation chainId, so after a chain fork two markets on different chains can have the same id.When selecting offers ("routing"), one should take into consideration the gas associated with their callbacks.Relies on the clz opcode (Osaka), on the mcopy, tload, and tstore opcodes (Cancun), and on the push0 opcode (Shanghai).

continuousFee(bytes32).details: The continuous fee is 0 until the market is created, then set to the default value.

enableLiquidationCursor(uint256).details: Enables a liquidationCursor for use at market creation. Liquidation cursors can only be enabled, never disabled. touchMarket checks the resulting maxLif for each market.liquidationCursor is required to be strictly below WAD so that maxLif's denominator (WAD - liquidationCursor * (WAD - lltv) / WAD) stays positive for every enabled lltv.

enableLltv(uint256).details: Enables a new LLTV tier. Tiers can only be enabled, never disabled.

isHealthy((uint256,address,address,(addr.details: This function should be called with the id corresponding to the market.This function does not call any oracle if debt is 0.Expects the id to correspond to the market's id.

liquidate((uint256,address,address,(addr.details: See LIQUIDATIONS section for more details.At least one of seizedAssets or repaidUnits should be equal to zero.Passing both 0 for seizedAssets and repaidUnits allows to realize bad debt with 0 token transferred.Liquidations with both 0 for seizedAssets and repaidUnits can be done with a collateral that is not activated.Returns the seized assets and the repaid units.

setMarketTickSpacing(bytes32,uint256).details: Refines the tick spacing of a market. Cannot increase (more ticks become accessible).

settlementFee(bytes32,uint256).details: Returns the settlement fee using piecewise linear interpolation between breakpoints.

settlementFeeCbps(bytes32).details: The settlement fee cbp values are 0 until the market is created, then set to the default value.

supplyCollateral((uint256,address,addres.details: This function checks authorization to prevent activated collateral poisoning.

take(((uint256,address,address,(address,.details: The taker might not get the price they expected if the settlement fee was just changed. A smart-contract can be used to perform atomic price checks.Taking buy offers with price < settlement fee will revert.In particular, if the settlement fee gets increased, it might implicitly cancel offers with very low price.All sellerAssets are reachable with the units input, and all buyerAssets are reachable only if buyerPrice <= WAD.The seller cannot be liquidated during the callbacks of a take.When onSell is called, the onBuy callback may have changed the state of Midnight.Returns buyerAssets and sellerAssets.

toMarket(bytes32).details: Reverts if the id is not a valid id of a touched market.Returns the market corresponding to the given id.

touchMarket((uint256,address,address,(ad.details: Returns the market id and creates the market if it doesn't exist yet.

updatePosition((uint256,address,address,.details: Slashes the position and accrues the continuous fee.Returns the new credit, new pending fee, and accrued fee after having updated the position.

updatePositionView((uint256,address,addr.details: Expects the id to correspond to the market's id.Returns the new credit, new pending fee, and accrued fee after having updated the position.

withdrawCollateral((uint256,address,addr.details: This function does not call any oracle if the borrower has no debt.
